enonce_markdown: A typist enters thousands of words a day. After some months she feels pain and numbness in her wrists and fingers because the same small movements are repeated for long periods. What is this condition called?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Health problems are named after their cause: repeated small movements damage tendons and nerves, whereas screen use affects the eyes and sitting affects the back.

### Solution

Pain and numbness in wrists and fingers after long periods of repeated typing movements is **repetitive strain injury (RSI)**. Computer vision syndrome concerns the eyes, hearing loss concerns loud sound, and disc compression concerns the lower back from poor sitting posture.

enonce_markdown: State TWO physical safety hazards found in a school computer room and give one precaution for each.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A hazard is a source of possible harm; a precaution removes the hazard or reduces its effect.

### Solution

- **Trailing cables** can make people trip and can be pulled out of sockets. Precaution: route cables through trunking or under floor covers and keep walkways clear.
- **Overloaded power sockets** (many multi-way adapters) can overheat and start a fire. Precaution: use enough wall sockets, avoid chaining extension leads, and fit surge-protected power strips.
- (Other valid answers: drinks spilt near equipment, giving electric shock - ban food and drink; blocked fire exits - keep them clear and signed.)

Mark scheme: 1 mark for each hazard and 1 mark for each precaution that matches it.

enonce_markdown: A computer room in Bamenda has its windows behind the monitors. By mid-afternoon many students complain of headaches and tired, watering eyes. Which single change would best deal with the cause?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Match the remedy to the symptom: headaches and eye strain come from glare and reflections on the screen, not from the hands, the back or software.

### Solution

Bright windows cause **glare and reflections**, which force the eyes to work harder and give headaches and eye strain. Blinds and screens placed at right angles to the windows remove the glare. Wrist rests help with RSI, a seat that leaves the feet off the floor is itself poor posture, and antivirus software has no effect on eye comfort.

choix.texte: Give each student a wrist rest for the keyboard
Install an antivirus program on every computer
Raise the seat height so that the feet no longer touch the floor
Fit blinds and turn the screens to stand at right angles to the windows

enonce_markdown: An office policy states that each 60-minute period of a data-entry shift is made of 50 minutes of work followed by a 10-minute rest away from the keyboard. How many minutes of actual work are done in an 8-hour shift?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Work out the length of one complete cycle, count the cycles in the shift, then multiply by the working part of a cycle.

### Solution

One cycle is 60 min, so 8 h = 480 min contains 480 / 60 = 8 cycles. Working time = 8 x 50 = **400 min**. Common errors: 410 (forgetting the rest after the last block), 470 (subtracting a single 10-minute rest only) and 440 (counting only 4 rests).

enonce_markdown: A fire starts in an electrical cabinet of a server room while the equipment is still powered. Which type of extinguisher is the most suitable?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Choose an extinguishing agent that does not conduct electricity and does not leave a residue that damages electronics.

### Solution

**Carbon dioxide** is non-conductive and leaves no residue, so it is suitable for live electrical equipment. Water and water-based foam conduct electricity and risk electric shock and further damage; wet chemical extinguishers are made for cooking oil and fat fires.

enonce_markdown:
A call centre in Douala has 30 operators who use headsets and PCs for 8 hours a day. Over six months the manager records many complaints: back and neck pain, tired and dry eyes, and pain in the wrists. The room is hot and the desks are at a fixed height.

For THREE of these problems, identify its likely cause in the workplace and recommend a measure. Then explain why an employer should also provide staff training and not only new equipment.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Link each symptom to its cause in the workstation (posture, screen, repeated movement, environment), then propose a measure that removes that cause; equipment only works if people use it correctly.

### Solution

| Problem | Likely cause | Measure |
|---|---|---|
| Back and neck pain | Fixed-height desks and chairs without support force a bent posture | Adjustable chairs with lumbar support, adjustable desks or monitor risers so that the top of the screen is at eye level |
| Tired, dry eyes | Long unbroken screen time, poor lighting or glare, heat that dries the eyes | Regular screen breaks (for example look away for 20 seconds every 20 minutes), anti-glare screens, correct brightness, cooler and ventilated room |
| Wrist pain (RSI) | Constant typing and mouse use with bent wrists | Ergonomic keyboard and mouse, wrist rests, scheduled breaks and task rotation |

**Why training is needed.** Adjustable furniture only helps if operators know how to set it to their own body, how to sit correctly, and why breaks matter; without training the equipment is left in the wrong position or the breaks are skipped, so the cost is wasted and the risk stays. Training also lets staff report early symptoms before they become long-term injuries, which reduces absence and compensation claims.
